newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply, data focus for week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply, data focus for week.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged at midday in extremely quiet action, traders said Monday.
"It's very quiet and we're unchanged from Friday," one trader said.

The supply picture, which has been bleak since the Christmas holidays, is beginning to improve this week, with about $3 billion of new issues on the calendar, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Despite the pickup, one trader said his focus for the week was on Friday's release of the producer price index for January. A survey of economists for Reuters showed expectations of a 0.3 percent rise overall and a 0.2 percent increase at the core rate.

Ahead of PPI is Tuesday's start of the Treasury's quarterly refunding, with the the sale of $17.75 billion of three-year notes. On Wednesday comes a $12 billion 10-year sale, and a $10 billion 30-year sale on Thursday.
In new issue pricings Monday, Dain Bosworth Inc said it tentatively priced $65.5 million Grand Forks, N.D., bonds at a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2029.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 7/32 to 116-5/32 while March T-bonds rose 5/32 to 112-20/32. The MOB spread was 113 ticks, compared to 111 at the close on Friday.

In the secondary market, bids on Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were up two basis points to 5.64 percent net. Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 lost one basis point, moving to 5.74 percent net after being quoted earlier Monday at a 5.77 percent.
